title: Ramstein defence meeting ends without a German decision on Leopard 2 tanks
body:
On 20 January 2023 defence ministers from about 50 countries met at Ramstein Air Base in southwestern Germany for the eighth Ukraine Defense Contact Group meeting since Russia's full-scale invasion began on 24 February 2022. German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius hosted the discussion. Berlin made no decision on supplying Leopard 2 tanks to Ukraine.

Ukrainian Defence Minister Oleksii Reznikov listed three priorities: air defence, heavy weapons such as tanks and howitzers, and steady ammunition supplies, and he also stressed repair services. President Volodymyr Zelensky made direct appeals for tanks. Pistorius said he was very sure there would be a decision in the short term, though he did not know what form it would take. He said Germany could act straight away if it approved Leopard transfers and that he had asked his ministry to review Germany's Leopard stocks.

On 19 January nine European nations had committed new aid packages, known as the Tallinn Pledge, including tanks, heavy artillery, infantry fighting vehicles, ammunition and air defence. France and the United Kingdom had already pledged to supply tanks. Polish Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki said on 19 January that Poland could supply Leopards regardless of Berlin's position. Pressure grew on Germany either to provide Leopards itself or to clear the way for countries such as Poland to transfer theirs. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on 20 January that Western tanks would not fundamentally change anything. Germany announced its Leopard decision five days later, on 25 January.
